reference: I. Krasikov, J. C. Lagarias, Bounds for the 3x+1 problem using difference inequalities, Acta Arith. 109 (2003) 237-258, arXiv:math/0205002, Thm 2.2
claim: L^NT_12(lambda) is INFEASIBLE for lambda = 1.80644: F(C) < C strictly for the positive vector C with coefficients rounded up, so lambda_k < lambda (no feasible point exists)
check: UPPER (infeasibility) certificate: same rows as below but with q = ceil(D lambda^-2), L2 >= D lambda^(alpha-2), L1 >= D lambda^(alpha-1) (rigorous upper bounds) and the STRICT reverse inequality q*C[(4i+2) mod N] + L*cbar(r) < C[i]*D for every i. The integer vector is C[i] = c[i] * 2^b, c read from c_f32.npy (float32); every C[i] must be an exact integer >= 1. Index i in [0, N) is the residue m = 3i+2 mod 3^k, n3 = N/3. For every i, with j, t = divmod(i, 3), cbar(r) = min(C[r], C[r+n3], C[r+2n3]): C[i]*D <= q*C[(4i+2) mod N] + L*cbar(r), where L = L2, r = 4j mod n3 if t = 0; L = 0 if t = 1; L = L1, r = (2j+1) mod n3 if t = 2. Requires q/D <= lambda^-2, L2/D <= lambda^(alpha-2), L1/D <= lambda^(alpha-1), alpha = log2(3).
